key_insight: Chronicle is an explainable transformer that uses entire irregular cancer care timelines to deliver continuously updated, patient-specific risk predictions across many cancer types and outcomes.
clinical_relevance: It may help clinicians better stratify risk and support individualized treatment planning by combining prognostic signals from diagnoses, treatments, labs, complications, and transfusions over time.
method: Trained on 53.7 million longitudinal data points from 51,711 patients across 67 cancer types.
Learns directly from irregular treatment timelines without imputation.
Jointly predicts eight clinical endpoints with built-in explainability.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, Chronicle outperformed cross-sectional survival models (C-index 0.84 vs 0.76-0.79), improved stratification over TNM stage, and achieved AUCs of 0.80-0.92 for seven adverse event and transfusion outcomes.
watch_item: Although it generalized across three healthcare systems, real-world deployment will still need local validation, workflow integration, and careful monitoring for site-specific data differences.
paper_title: An explainable transformer model learning from entire treatment timelines for pan-cancer risk profiling across healthcare systems
